trees.title: The engine is losing power
trees.summary: The car doesn't respond normally to the accelerator — weak, sluggish, or “stuttering”.
trees.safety: Sudden power loss right after driving through a deep puddle, or a flashing “check engine” light, are reasons to stop immediately and not keep driving.

n1.q: When do you feel the power loss?

options.label: Only on hills or under quick acceleration, and it's fine during normal driving
The engine “stutters,” cuts out for a moment and responds again

n2.q: Has a “check engine” light come on?

n3.q: When did you last service the air filter or the fuel filter?

options.label: A long time ago, not sure exactly when

n5.q: Did this happen right after driving through a deep puddle or a flooded area?

r-boost-loss.result: Suspected drop in turbo boost pressure
r-boost-loss.text: Power loss only on hills or under quick acceleration, when the engine feels fine during normal driving, points to a drop in turbo boost pressure — for example a disconnected or leaking air hose, or a faulty bypass valve.
actions: Go to a garage for a check; a drop in turbo pressure isn't immediately dangerous, but it hurts power and fuel economy.
Avoid overtaking that needs strong acceleration until it's checked.

r-misfire.text: The engine “stuttering,” cutting out for a moment and responding again, mainly under acceleration, points to a cylinder not firing properly — a weak spark plug, an ignition coil, or a clogged fuel injector.
actions: Go to a garage for a computerised diagnosis.
Driving for long with a misfire can damage the catalytic converter.

r-check-engine-power.result: Check engine light on together with power loss
r-check-engine-power.text: A steady check engine light, together with a noticeable drop in power, points to a fault the car's computer has detected, deliberately limiting engine performance in response, to prevent damage.
actions: Go to a garage soon for a computerised diagnosis.
Drive carefully and avoid sharp acceleration until it's checked.

r-misfire-severe.result: Flashing “check engine” light — a severe misfire
r-misfire-severe.text: A flashing light, unlike a steady one, indicates a severe misfire that can send unburnt fuel into the catalytic converter and destroy it within minutes.
actions: Slow down immediately, avoid accelerating, and stop as soon as possible in a safe place.
Don't keep driving with heavy acceleration until it's checked.

r-clogged-filter.result: Suspected clogged air filter or fuel filter
r-clogged-filter.text: Gradual power loss, without a warning light and without engine stuttering, developing over time, is often linked to a dirty air filter restricting airflow, or a clogged fuel filter.
actions: Check and replace the air filter according to the schedule in the owner's manual.
If replacing it doesn't solve it, go to a garage for a further check.

r-turbo-or-sensor.result: Suspected sensor or turbo, not the filters
r-turbo-or-sensor.text: Gradual power loss, when the filters have been serviced recently, points more to a sensor giving the engine computer a wrong reading (like a mass airflow sensor), or a turbo starting to wear.
actions: Go to a garage for a computerised diagnosis — reading the fault codes will narrow down the suspects quickly.

r-hydrolock-water.result: Suspected water ingestion into the engine
r-hydrolock-water.text: Sudden power loss right after driving through a deep puddle or a flood is a serious suspicion of water getting into the engine — water doesn't compress like air, and can break internal parts if the engine keeps running.
actions: Switch off the engine immediately and don't try to restart it.
Call for a tow to a garage; there's no roadside fix for this.

r-sudden-check.result: Sudden power loss — needs an immediate check
r-sudden-check.text: Sharp, sudden power loss, unrelated to flooding, can stem from a range of causes — from a failed sensor to a fuel problem — and is hard to narrow down without a diagnostic computer.
actions: Drive carefully to the nearest garage, or call for a tow if the problem is severe.
Don't continue on a long drive or at high speed until it's checked.
